title: Exceptions & testing
outcome: Handle faults explicitly and write tests that expose incorrect behavior.

steps.title: 1. Catch expected failures
steps.text: A failed conversion should not conceal a programming defect. Catch the specific expected exception, and keep the try block close to the operation that can fail.

steps.title: 2. Raise meaningful errors
steps.text: Return a normal result for a normal case; raise an exception for a contract violation. Exception chaining can retain the underlying cause when translating errors.

steps.title: 3. Clean up on every path
steps.text: finally runs whether the operation returns or raises. Context managers express scoped resource ownership. Do not replace the original exception accidentally during cleanup.

steps.title: 4. Retry only the specified condition
steps.text: Retry transient failures only, with a bounded attempt count. In drills, fake callables replace devices; no sleep or live network access is required. Permanent failures propagate.

steps.title: 5. Test a defect, not a happy screenshot
steps.text: A useful test accepts a correct implementation and rejects a seeded defect. Run your test against both. Passing these cases is evidence about tested behavior, not proof of exhaustive correctness.

contract: Define parse(text). Return int(text) for valid text, None for ValueError. Other exception types must propagate.

tasks.title: Bounded transient retries
contract: Define retry(operation, attempts=3). attempts must be an int (not bool) >=1 or raise ValueError.
Call until success, retrying TimeoutError only. Re-raise the final TimeoutError if all attempts fail. No sleep.
hints: Identify what must change and what must stay unchanged in this task: bounded transient retries.
Bound the number of calls, validate the attempt count first, and retry only the specified transient failure.
Compare the implementation with case 04-invalid attempts. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.

tasks.title: Test a boundary defect
tasks.brief: Write tests against a supplied function.
contract: Define verify(candidate). candidate(value) should return True exactly for integers in [1,4094], including both endpoints. Inputs here are integers only.
Your function returns True if all your probes match that contract, False on mismatch or exception. It must reject the supplied boundary mutants.
hints: Identify what must change and what must stay unchanged in this task: test a boundary defect.
Test the two endpoints and their immediate neighbors against the candidate, not only a middle value.
Compare the implementation with case 04-always false. Trace the supplied inputs and the exact return/output type before changing the code.
